subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured credential-shaped `skills.entries.<skill>.env` names be admitted for intended active-skill host exec use, and where should unrelated generic exec strip those same active skill secrets?
rationale: The reported behavior contradicts documented host-run skill env injection, but the repair changes a credential-to-exec boundary and overlaps the inverse secret-leak issue.

options.title: Scoped skill credential delivery
options.body: Permit only explicitly configured keys for the intended active skill path, keep dangerous host/runtime names blocked, and strip active skill secrets from unrelated generic exec children.

options.title: Metadata-only sensitive allowlist
options.body: Keep the current sanitizer behavior and update docs or skill metadata requirements so arbitrary credential-shaped `skills.entries.*.env` names are not promised.

options.title: Defer to a new secret contract
options.body: Leave the sanitizer unchanged until maintainers define a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills needing headless auth.

recommendation.title: Scoped skill credential delivery
recommendation.body: Permit only explicitly configured keys for the intended active skill path, keep dangerous host/runtime names blocked, and strip active skill secrets from unrelated generic exec children.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a host exec credential-boundary decision, and joshavant authored the current host exec env hardening path.
